IN NO EVENT SHALL THE COPYRIGHT HOLDER OR CONTRIBUTORS BE LIABLE FOR * ANY DIRECT, INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, EXEMPLARY, OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES * (INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, PROCUREMENT OF SUBSTITUTE GOODS OR SERVICES; * LOSS OF USE, DATA, OR PROFITS; OR BUSINESS INTERRUPTION) HOWEVER CAUSED AND ON * ANY THEORY OF LIABILITY, WHETHER IN CONTRACT, STRICT LIABILITY, OR TORT * (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE OR OTHERWISE) ARISING IN ANY WAY OUT OF THE USE OF THIS * SOFTWARE, EVEN IF ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGE. */ package nz.tate.timezonehud; import net.runelite.api.MessageNode; import net.runelite.api.events.ChatMessage; /** * Replaces the text of a chat message that has already arrived, so that a * {@code !TZ} line reads as its answer in this client. * *

Why it is done this way, and why it must stay this way

* * Jagex's third-party client guidelines, which RuneLite enforces, forbid two things that a * "!TZ converter" could very easily be built out of: * *
    *
  • No modifying outgoing chat messages after the user sends them.
    • *
  • No autotyping -- a plugin must never put text into the chatbox input.
    • *
* *

This class does neither. By the time it runs, the message has already been sent to * Jagex's servers, exactly as the user typed it, and has come back as an ordinary received * chat message. What is edited is the {@link MessageNode} of that received message -- the * client-side record of what to draw. The bytes on the wire were never touched, other * players see the raw {@code !TZ} line, and only people running this plugin see the answer. * This is the same mechanism core RuneLite's {@code !kc} and {@code !pb} use. * *

Do not "simplify" this into the ChatInput path. {@code ChatCommandManager} also * accepts a {@code BiPredicate} that runs before the message is * sent and can call {@code chatboxInput.consume()} to swallow or alter it. That would be * shorter and it would be modifying an outgoing message. D4 rejects it explicitly. Equally, * never write the answer into the chatbox input: that is autotyping, whatever the intent. */ final class ChatDisplayRewriter { private ChatDisplayRewriter() { } /** * Swaps the displayed text of an already-received message for the response. * *

Only a successful conversion is worth replacing a public line with. If the command * was malformed the message is left exactly as everyone else sees it, because silently * turning someone's public message into an error message in their own client is worse * than saying nothing. * * @return true if the display was changed, so the caller knows to refresh the chat */ static boolean rewrite(ChatMessage chatMessage, CommandResponse response) { if (!response.isConversion()) { return false; } MessageNode node = chatMessage.getMessageNode(); if (node == null) { return false; } node.setValue(response.getText()); return true; } }

This exists so {@link ConfigClockStore} can be unit tested against a plain map. * ConfigManager is a concrete class wired into a running client and cannot be stood up in a * test, and the store's real job -- turning clocks into text and back -- is worth testing. */ public interface ConfigValues { /** * @return the saved value, or null if nothing has been saved under this key */ String get(String key); void put(String key, String value); }

IN NO EVENT SHALL THE COPYRIGHT HOLDER OR CONTRIBUTORS BE LIABLE FOR * ANY DIRECT, INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, EXEMPLARY, OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES * (INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, PROCUREMENT OF SUBSTITUTE GOODS OR SERVICES; * LOSS OF USE, DATA, OR PROFITS; OR BUSINESS INTERRUPTION) HOWEVER CAUSED AND ON * ANY THEORY OF LIABILITY, WHETHER IN CONTRACT, STRICT LIABILITY, OR TORT * (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE OR OTHERWISE) ARISING IN ANY WAY OUT OF THE USE OF THIS * SOFTWARE, EVEN IF ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGE. */ package nz.tate.timezonehud.core; import java.util.List; /** * Where the clock list lives between sessions. * *

This is the seam between the pure core and RuneLite: {@link ClockRepository} owns the * rules (ordering, seeding, the first-run flag) and knows nothing about how any of it is * written down. The ConfigManager-backed implementation arrives with the config interface. * *

The seeded flag is stored separately from the list on purpose. D10 requires seeding to * happen exactly once, guarded by a flag rather than by "is the list empty" -- otherwise a * user who deliberately clears every clock gets Local and Jagex back on the next start. */ public interface ClockStore { /** * @return the saved clocks in display order; empty if there are none */ List loadClocks(); void saveClocks(List clocks); /** * @return true once seeding has happened, whether or not the clocks survived */ boolean isSeeded(); void markSeeded(); }
